title: Government Strengthens Cyber Security Preparedness of Central Government Digital Platforms and Citizen Services
body_text:
The Government is committed to ensuring an open, safe, trusted and accountable cyberspace. Several legal, technical and administrative policy measures have been implemented to strengthen the cyber security preparedness of Central Government digital platforms and citizen service portals, protect digital infrastructure and enhance cyber resilience.
Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) has been designated as the national agency for responding to cyber security incidents under Section 70B of the Information Technology Act, 2000.
As per the information reported to and tracked by CERT-In, the total number of cyber security incidents observed during the last three years are given below:
Year No of incidents 2023 15,92,917 2024 20,41,360 2025 29,44,248
On observing cyber security incidents including those related to Government-managed platforms, CERT-In advises remedial measures to concerned organizations and coordinates incident response measures with affected organizations, service providers, respective sector regulators as well as Law Enforcement Agencies.
The Government has institutionalized a nationwide integrated and coordinated system to deal with cyber-attacks in the country. These measures, inter alia, include:
a.   National Cyber Security Coordinator (NCSC) under the National Security Council Secretariat (NSCS) to ensure coordination related to cyber security amongst different agencies.
b.   National Cyber Coordination Centre (NCCC), implemented by CERT-In, examines cyberspace to detect cyber security threats and shares threat intelligence with concerned organisations, State Governments and stakeholder agencies for taking appropriate action.
c.   National Critical Information Infrastructure Protection Centre (NCIIPC) has been established under Section 70A of the Information Technology Act, 2000 for protection of Critical Information Infrastructure (CII).
d.   NCIIPC provides near real-time threat intelligence and situational awareness, issues regular alerts and advisories to Critical Information Infrastructure (CII)/Protected System (PS) entities, periodically undertakes vulnerability and risk assessment of CII/Protected Systems and provides feedback to the concerned entities.
e.    Cyber Swachhta Kendra (CSK)
A citizen-centric service provided by CERT-In, which extends the vision of Swachh Bharat to the Cyber Space. It is the Botnet Cleaning and Malware Analysis Centre and helps to detect malicious programs and provides free tools to remove the same. It also provides cyber security tips and best practices for citizens and organisations.
f.      Sectoral Computer Security Incident Response Team (CSIRT)
CSIRT in the Finance sector (CSIRT-Fin) under CERT-In is operational since May 2022 to coordinate cyber incident response in the banking and financial sector. CSIRT-Power has been operational since September 2024 as an extended arm of CERT-In to coordinate cyber security issues within the power sector entities.
g.  CERT-In operates an automated cyber threat intelligence exchange platform for sharing tailored alerts with organisations across sectors for proactive threat mitigation.
h.   CERT-In has formulated a Cyber Crisis Management Plan (CCMP) for countering cyber-attacks and cyber terrorism for implementation by all Ministries/Departments, State Governments and their organizations.
i.     Cyber security mock drills are conducted regularly by CERT-In, to enable assessment of cyber security posture and preparedness of organisations in Government and critical sectors.
j.   CERT-In has created a panel of 'Information Security Auditing Organisations' for auditing, including vulnerability assessment and penetration testing of computer systems, networks, websites and applications of various organizations of the Government and critical sectors. 237 information security auditing organisations are empanelled by CERT-In to support and audit implementation of Information Security Best Practices.
k.   All the Government websites and applications are audited with respect to cyber security prior to their hosting.  The auditing of the websites and applications is conducted on a regular basis after hosting also.
l.    CERT-In issues alerts and advisories regarding latest cyber threats/vulnerabilities and countermeasures to protect computers, networks and data on an ongoing basis.
m.  The Government has put in place a statutory framework under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. The rules framed, thereunder, to ensure that the sharing and processing of citizens’ digital personal data for law enforcement purposes is undertaken in a lawful, secure and accountable manner.
n. Information Security Education and Awareness (ISEA) Workshops
●    The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) is implementing the ISEA project for generating human resources in Information Security and creating general awareness on various aspects of cyber hygiene & cyber security among the masses.
●     6,650 awareness workshops have been conducted across the country covering over 11.37 lakh participants, including students, teachers, law enforcement personnel, Government officials, and the general public. This includes 70 awareness workshops organized in Kerala covering 9481 participants
●     Further, multilingual awareness material in the form of handbooks, short videos, posters, brochures, cartoon stories for children, etc. published and disseminated through print, electronics, social media, and www.isea.gov.in & https://staysafeonline.in/ .
o. National Cyber Security Awareness Activities
●    The Government organises events and activities for citizens as well as the technical cyber community across the country. Some of these include:
●        National Cyber Security Awareness Month (NCSAM) in October every year
●        Safer Internet Day on the second Tuesday of February
●        Swachhta Pakhwada (1st –15th February), and
●        Cyber Jagrookta Diwas (CJD) on the first Wednesday of every month
p. Training programs by CERT-In
●  CERT-In conducts cyber security training programs in collaboration with Industry partners to upskill the cyber security workforce in Government, public and private organizations. 32 and 13 training programs were conducted covering 20799 and 12109 participants including 786 and 411 participants from Kerala during the year 2025 and 2026 (upto June) respectively
●    CERT-In is regularly sharing safety and security tips and awareness posters, info-graphics and videos through its official websites and social media handles such as Facebook, X(Twitter), Instagram, YouTube and LinkedIn for sensitizing internet users on cyber security attacks and frauds and prevention measures.
This information was given by Union Minister of State for Electronics and IT Shri Jitin Prasada in Lok Sabha on 12.08.2026
****
Vinod Kumar / Kanishk Sharma

enrichment.summary: In a Lok Sabha reply on 12 August 2026, MoS Electronics & IT Jitin Prasada detailed India's cyber security architecture for government digital platforms, citing CERT-In as the statutory nodal incident response agency under Section 70B of the IT Act. He noted cyber incidents rose from 15,92,917 in 2023 to 20,41,360 in 2024 to 29,44,248 in 2025, and listed institutional mechanisms including NCSC, NCCC, NCIIPC, sectoral CSIRTs (Finance, Power), Cyber Swachhta Kendra, and awareness/training programmes under ISEA and CERT-In.
enrichment.context:
Cyber security governance in India rests on the Information Technology Act, 2000, particularly Sections 70A (Critical Information Infrastructure protection via NCIIPC) and 70B (CERT-In as national incident response agency). Over the past decade, India has layered institutions—NCSC under NSCS for high-level coordination, NCCC for threat detection, and sector-specific CSIRTs for Finance and Power—onto this statutory base, reflecting growing recognition of cyber threats to critical infrastructure. The steep rise in reported incidents (nearly doubling from 2023 to 2025) underscores the scale of India's digital exposure as e-governance and financial digitisation expand under Digital India.

The reply also references the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, whose rules govern lawful processing of citizens' data for law enforcement, situating cyber security within the broader data protection and privacy framework established after the Puttaswamy judgment. Awareness and capacity-building efforts like ISEA, Cyber Jagrookta Diwas, and Safer Internet Day represent the citizen-facing dimension of this strategy, aiming to build a 'digitally aware' populace alongside institutional cyber defence.

prelims_questions.question: Under which section of the Information Technology Act, 2000 is CERT-In designated as the national agency for responding to cyber security incidents?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states CERT-In is designated as the national incident response agency under Section 70B of the IT Act, 2000, while Section 70A relates to NCIIPC's establishment for Critical Information Infrastructure protection.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following bodies operates as a sectoral Computer Security Incident Response Team (CSIRT) for the banking and financial sector under CERT-In?
prelims_questions.explanation: CSIRT-Fin, operational since May 2022 under CERT-In, coordinates cyber incident response specifically in the banking and financial sector, as mentioned in the release.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the institutional architecture for cyber security governance in India. In light of the sharply rising number of cyber incidents, examine the adequacy of existing mechanisms like CERT-In, NCIIPC, and sectoral CSIRTs in protecting critical digital infrastructure.
mains_questions.gs_paper: GS Paper 3 - Internal Security/Science and Technology

mains_questions.question: Critically analyse how the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 interacts with cyber security frameworks in ensuring accountable processing of citizens' data, particularly in the context of law enforcement access.

study_notes.reason: The release provides a testable institutional map of India's cyber security architecture (CERT-In, NCIIPC, NCSC, statutory sections) alongside real analytical material on the sharply rising incident trend and the adequacy of institutional response, giving it genuine dual value.

prelims.point: CERT-In is the national nodal agency for cyber security incident response, designated under Section 70B of the IT Act, 2000.
prelims.why_important: A core statutory fact frequently tested - agency name, parent Act, and specific section must be matched correctly.

prelims.point: NCIIPC was established under Section 70A of the IT Act, 2000, for protection of Critical Information Infrastructure (CII).
prelims.why_important: UPSC often tests the distinction between Section 70A (NCIIPC/CII protection) and Section 70B (CERT-In/incident response).

prelims.point: National Cyber Security Coordinator (NCSC) functions under the National Security Council Secretariat (NSCS), not under MeitY.
prelims.why_important: Tests knowledge of which parent body coordinates cyber security policy at the apex level.

prelims.point: National Cyber Coordination Centre (NCCC) is implemented by CERT-In to detect threats and share intelligence.
prelims.why_important: A commonly confused institution with NCSC and NCIIPC; distinguishing their functions is examinable.

prelims.point: Sectoral CSIRTs exist for Finance (since May 2022) and Power (since September 2024), both operating under CERT-In.
prelims.why_important: Specific sector-agency pairing and start dates are the kind of detail UPSC uses to construct 'match the following' items.

prelims.point: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 provides the statutory framework for lawful processing of citizens' data, including for law enforcement purposes.
prelims.why_important: A key recent legislation whose scope and linkage to cyber governance is a recurring prelims theme.

mains.point: Cyber incidents nearly doubled from ~15.9 lakh (2023) to ~29.4 lakh (2025), reflecting the scale of India's growing digital exposure under Digital India and e-governance expansion.
mains.analytical_use: Used to substantiate arguments on why cyber security must keep pace with digitisation in questions on internal security or e-governance risks.

mains.point: India's cyber security architecture is fragmented across multiple bodies (NCSC, NCCC, NCIIPC, CERT-In, sectoral CSIRTs), raising questions of coordination and overlap.
mains.analytical_use: Deployed in 'critically examine' questions on whether India's multi-agency cyber governance model ensures effective coordination or creates silos.

mains.point: Reliance on citizen awareness programmes (ISEA, Cyber Jagrookta Diwas, Safer Internet Day) suggests government response leans on capacity-building rather than only technical/legal deterrence.
mains.analytical_use: Useful for 'suggest measures' questions on strengthening cyber security preparedness beyond institutional mechanisms.

mains.point: Protection of Critical Information Infrastructure (via NCIIPC) is central to safeguarding sectors like power and finance from cyber-attacks with national security implications.
mains.analytical_use: Applicable to questions on internal security threats to critical infrastructure and the adequacy of India's protective mechanisms.

both.concept: CERT-In's statutory mandate under Section 70B combined with its expanding operational role (mock drills, CCMP, threat intelligence sharing) amid rising incidents
both.prelims_angle: Tests the specific statutory basis and named functions of CERT-In.
both.mains_angle: Allows analysis of whether CERT-In's expanding informal/operational mandate is adequate given the scale of incident growth, and whether statutory backing needs strengthening.

low_priority.point: Specific figures on Kerala-related workshop participation (70 workshops, 9,481 participants) and training numbers for 2025/2026.
low_priority.reason: State-specific administrative statistics with no conceptual or policy significance for exam purposes.

low_priority.point: Mention of Swachhta Pakhwada and NCSAM as awareness calendar events.
low_priority.reason: Ceremonial/calendar-based activities without substantive policy content.

low_priority.point: Count of 237 empanelled information security auditing organisations.
low_priority.reason: A minor administrative figure unlikely to be tested and lacking analytical value.
